solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Criminal made rough arrangement for defence

indicators.note: something criminal is bent or crooked, so these letters are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: A shady deal is roughly cobbled together, as if a crook drew up the security plan.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Guard was Britain's volunteer local defence force in the Second World War.
explanation.definitionFit: The wartime volunteer militia was organised as a home defence measure, so it is an arrangement for defence.

clue.text: Covering hospital, I give injections

parts.note: H is the standard abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs
to jab is to give someone a jab, an injection

explanation.surface: A nurse in a hospital describes her job of giving injections, perhaps while covered up.
explanation.definitionFit: The headscarf worn by many Muslim women is a covering for the head and neck.

clue.text: President Danton, at first in his own house?

indicators.note: in says the first letter of Danton is placed inside the word for house

parts.note: maison is French for house, apt for the French revolutionary Danton

indicators.note: at first asks for only the opening letter of Danton

explanation.surface: Imagines the French revolutionary Danton as a president, at home in his own house.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the French: Danton would call his house his MAISON.
explanation.definitionFit: James Madison was the fourth President of the United States.

clue.text: One length in longitude out? Bill could be

indicators.note: out means put out of order, so these letters are shuffled

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: Sounds like a navigator's error: one unit of length out in a longitude reading.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is only a link here. In Parliament a bill is guillotined when debate on it is cut short by a timetable motion.
explanation.definitionFit: Parliamentary procedure lets the government cut debate on legislation short, which is what happens to a bill under the guillotine.

clue.text: A lot to carry is commonly dangerous

indicators.note: commonly signals a dropped H, as in casual or Cockney speech

parts.note: harmful means dangerous

explanation.surface: Warns that a heavy load is, as people say in casual speech, dangerous to lift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'commonly' marks dropping the initial H, the way a Cockney says 'armful for harmful.
explanation.definitionFit: An amount held in the arms is a large quantity to carry.

clue.text: So gorgeous, come to sudden end

definitions.meaning: ... gorgeous means stunningly attractive, the first word intensifying the second
to die suddenly and without warning

explanation.surface: Something beautiful meets an abrupt end.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase works both as an intensifier of stunning looks and as a verb for dying abruptly.

clue.text: Squeeze puts pressure on silent type

indicators.note: on means placed after, so the pressure letter follows the silent type

parts.note: someone who clams up says nothing, a clam
P is the symbol for pressure in physics

explanation.surface: A bully squeezes a quiet person, leaning on the silent type.
explanation.definitionFit: A clamp is a device that grips things tight, so to clamp is to squeeze.

clue.text: Wound workers up

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the letters are read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: the TUC, Trades Union Congress, is the British federation of workers' unions

explanation.surface: Workers get wound up, angry and agitated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wound' reads as wound up, annoyed; it is the injury. The TUC is Britain's Trades Union Congress.
explanation.definitionFit: A gash in the skin is an injury, so the noun is a synonym for a wound.

clue.text: Put to practical use, program wasn't accurate

parts.note: an app is a computer program
lied means told something untrue

explanation.surface: Software was put into use but gave inaccurate results.
explanation.definitionFit: Applied science or skill is knowledge put to practical use.

clue.text: Beyond nervous, maybe frightened or terrified

parts.note: past means beyond, as in past the church
tense means nervous

explanation.surface: Someone is so nervous they are beyond nerves, frightened or terrified.
explanation.walkthrough: 'frightened or terrified' looks like a state of mind but is grammatical: both are verbs in the past tense.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are verb forms in the grammatical tense for completed actions, so they are examples of it.

clue.text: Almost bound to accept platform for belief

indicators.note: to accept means to take something in, so one word goes inside another
almost means the word is short of its last letter

parts.note: a bound is a leap, a jump
a dais is a raised platform

explanation.surface: Someone almost committed to taking a stand for what they believe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bound' here is a leap, not tied or obliged; 'Almost' leaves JUM.
explanation.definitionFit: The religion of the Jewish people is a faith, a system of belief.

clue.text: Autumn work for army type

parts.note: October is an autumn month, abbreviated Oct
an opus is a musical or literary work

explanation.surface: Suggests a soldier's job in the autumn season.
explanation.walkthrough: 'army' sounds like soldiers but is read as arm-y: a creature with many arms.
explanation.definitionFit: The eight-limbed sea creature is a whimsically 'army' type, all arms.

clue.text: It has gears not fully engaged

indicators.note: not fully means the word lacks its last letter

parts.note: a phone line that is engaged is busy

explanation.surface: A machine whose gears are not fully meshed together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'engaged' looks like gear talk, but it means occupied: BUSY, cut short.
explanation.definitionFit: A road passenger vehicle has a gearbox, so it is something with gears.

clue.text: Set of tasks all industry processed

indicators.note: processed means worked over, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A to-do list processed by an entire industry.
explanation.definitionFit: A long itemised list of jobs to get through is idiomatically named after a list of washing.

clue.text: Dismiss clergyman, losing one church

parts.note: in cricket to york a batsman is to bowl him out with a yorker

indicators.note: losing means the letter for one is taken away

parts.note: a minister is a clergyman
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: A church fires one of its clergymen.
explanation.walkthrough: To york is cricket slang for dismissing a batsman with a yorker, a ball pitched at his feet. York Minster is the great cathedral in the city of York.
explanation.definitionFit: The cathedral in the northern English city is a church.

clue.text: My cold-blooded pet said to be tiny

indicators.note: said to be marks words spoken aloud for their sound

parts.note: a newt is a cold-blooded amphibian kept as a pet, so this is my newt

explanation.surface: Someone describes their pet reptile or amphibian as very small.
explanation.definitionFit: Pronounced my-NEWT, the adjective means extremely small.

clue.text: Given encouragement, doctor bound to include extra on bill

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, a doctor

indicators.note: to include means to hold within, so one word goes inside another

parts.note: tied means bound
VAT, value added tax, is added on to a bill

explanation.surface: A doctor is obliged to add a surcharge to a patient's bill.
explanation.walkthrough: VAT is the British sales tax added to bills.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone spurred on or given an incentive is motivated.

clue.text: Difficult to forget the last and worst point about nag

indicators.note: to forget the last means drop the final letter of the word

parts.note: hard means difficult

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: the nadir is the lowest or worst point

explanation.surface: Suggests it is hard to put the worst moment behind you when someone nags.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to forget the last' takes D off HARD; 'about' turns NADIR into RIDAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A harridan is a scolding, bossy old woman, and 'nag' names such a person.

clue.text: Very conical, explosive?

indicators.note: explosive means blown apart, so these letters are scattered

explanation.surface: Describes a steep cone-shaped mountain that might blow up.
explanation.definitionFit: A cone-shaped mountain that erupts is a volcano, so the whole clue describes something of that nature.

clue.text: Moving around in dry, unfinished opera

indicators.note: in says the anagram goes inside the letters for dry

parts.note: TT, teetotal, means not drinking alcohol, dry

indicators.note: moving means shifting around, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone wanders round, sober, in an opera that never got finished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moving' gives URANDO. 'unfinished' is part of the definition, not a deletion: Puccini died before completing this opera.
explanation.definitionFit: Puccini's last opera was left incomplete at his death and completed by Alfano, so it is an unfinished opera.

clue.text: With bread, soak up fish

parts.note: a roll is a small piece of bread
to mop is to soak up liquid

explanation.surface: Use some bread to soak up the sauce from a dish.
explanation.definitionFit: A rolled pickled herring fillet is a kind of fish dish.

clue.text: Perhaps I look unwell and spit

definitions.meaning: read as a sentence '...', a way of saying I look unwell
to skewer, as on a spit used for roasting

explanation.surface: Someone feels ill and spits.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading splits the word into I'M PALE.
explanation.definitionFit: To pierce with a sharp point is to skewer, which is what to spit means as a verb.

clue.text: One playing with current switch

parts.note: AC is alternating current
a switch is a tress or lock of hair

explanation.surface: Someone fiddles with a light switch while current flows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'switch' is not an electrical switch but a tress of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman who plays a role on stage or screen is a performer, one playing a part.

clue.text: In Russia, Michael has parking accident

parts.note: Misha is the Russian familiar form of Michael
P is the abbreviation for parking, as on signs

explanation.surface: A Russian named Michael has a parking accident.
explanation.definitionFit: A misfortune or unlucky incident is a minor accident.

clue.text: 'Farewell' — it's how they speak in the valleys?

parts.note: a vale is a valley
diction is a person's manner of speaking

explanation.surface: Jokes that Welsh valley dwellers have a special way of saying goodbye.
explanation.definitionFit: A valediction is a formal leave-taking, a saying of farewell.

clue.text: Boat only goes backwards

indicators.note: goes backwards tells us to read the letters in reverse

parts.note: but means only, as in 'but a child'

explanation.surface: A boat that can only go in reverse.
explanation.definitionFit: A tub is slang for a slow, clumsy boat.

clue.text: Stick no bill up

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the letters are read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: a tab is a bill, as in pick up the tab

explanation.surface: A notice forbids sticking bills up: no bill posting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stick no bill' echoes the old sign 'Stick no bills'.
explanation.definitionFit: A conductor's or relay runner's short rod is a stick.

clue.text: American native at home on county boundary

indicators.note: on means placed after, so the home word comes after the boundary

parts.note: the River Tamar forms most of the border between Devon and Cornwall
in means at home

explanation.surface: A Native American living at home right on the county line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at' looks like a piece but belongs to 'at home' for IN. The Tamar is the river dividing the English counties of Devon and Cornwall.
explanation.definitionFit: This small South American monkey is native to the Americas.

clue.text: County missing land got in frenzy

indicators.note: missing means without, so those letters are taken away

parts.note: Rutland is the smallest county in England

explanation.surface: A county that has lost land is thrown into a frenzy.
explanation.definitionFit: The rut is the mating season when male deer are in a state of frenzied excitement.

clue.text: Under pressure here, tries not to start to worry

indicators.note: not to start means drop the first letter of the word

parts.note: shots are tries, attempts
to eat at someone is to worry them

explanation.surface: Someone under pressure tries not to begin worrying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not to start' drops the S of SHOTS, leaving HOTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone in a position of tough scrutiny is under pressure, so this seat is where pressure is felt.

clue.text: Remove plant from container, maybe, in store

definitions.meaning: read as ..., to take a plant out of its pot

explanation.surface: A gardener repots a plant in a storeroom.
explanation.definitionFit: A warehouse or storage building is a store.

clue.text: Rich clothing around Juliet's intended, nothing new

parts.note: ca, circa, means around
in Romeo and Juliet, Count Paris is the man Juliet's family intend her to marry
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Juliet's fiancé, who has nothing new to wear, is dressed in rich clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Ornamental trappings for a horse, or fine dress, are rich clothing.
